newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's BUX dips, futures end weaker.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's BUX dips, futures end weaker.

text.p: Hungarian shares traded sideways pulling the BUX index a shade down on Thursday following Wednesday'd dip on Wall Street which seems to be the main driving factor these days beside the dollar, traders said.
The BUX index finished at 5,464.77 points, down 16.88.
"Earlier this market was largely independent from movements of the Dow but in these days this is not true, we're heavily dependent on the Dow Jones," said Geza Raner of Bank Austria-Investment Rt.
BUX futures lost ground, easing by between 10 and 84.50 points. June BUX fell 22.50 points to 5,752.5.
Analysts saw the market's long-term outlook as positive but said the near-term outlook is slump with sideways movement seen continuing for several reasons.
"The first reason is that people have been occupied with what's going on in the United States," said Nigel Rendell, strategist at HSBC James Capel in London.

"With the interest rate rise a couple of weeks ago a lot of people have been reluctant to invest in not only in eastern Europe but also generally on world markets," he said. "So this kept people on the sidelines a little bit."
The Hungarian market had a strong run earlier this year with a February peak prompting profit-taking.
"There has obviously been a temptation to take profit and that impacted on the market as well," Rendell said.
A likely third factor was the Hungarian interest rates edged up.
"I don't think that started a new trend...but it had made one or two investors perhaps slightly cautious."

On Thursday, trading in oil company MOL shares revived with its volume rising to above 240,000 units as speculation has increased before the company's new phase of sell-off. MOL closed at 3,030, down 15.
Chemicals TVK remained in focus with its price adding 30 forints to 2,480.

The other chemicals firm, Borsodchem closed at 6,350 forints, down 70, before signing an agreement with Japan's Mitsui Toatsu and Chisso Engineering on the expansion of its methylene diphenyil diisocyanate capacity.
